Spatially resample the covariates and observations resources Spatially Resample Covariates and Observations Across Spatial Scales

Source: R/resample_covariates_and_observations.R
resample_covariates_and_observations.Rd

This function resamples covariate and observation data across spatial scales generated from the WildObsR::spatial_hexagon_generator() function. It validates the input data by ensuring that all necessary spatial, temporal, and deployment identifiers are present and correctly formatted. Numeric covariates are aggregated using means weighted by each deployment's camera-days (see weights), while categorical covariates are combined by concatenating unique values. Logical and factor columns in either table, such as baitUse and featureType from frictionless::read_resource(), keep their class (and factor levels) when every cell holds one value; where some cell holds several, the column is pasted as text, for example "FALSE - TRUE", with a message naming it. Modal columns always keep their class.

With obs = NULL, only the covariates are resampled, which is all the occupancy and abundance workflow needs, and is much faster (see "How the tables connect").

In addition, the function computes several key metrics:

  • Sampling effort per spatial unit (trap-nights),

  • Resampled start and end dates for each sampling unit.

Users can optionally specify which covariate columns should be aggregated using the mode (i.e., the most frequent value) instead of concatenation, and which covariate variables that vary in space and time (i.e., observation covariates) should be incorporated into the resampled observations. Example values provided in the documentation (c("habitat") for mode aggregation and c("baitUse", "featureType") for observation covariates) serve as examples that work with any camtrap DP formatted data.

The function generates new columns in the output data as follows:

Resampled Covariates include:

deploymentsIncluded

A concatenated string of deploymentID values representing all deployments included within each spatial cell.

cellEffort

The total sampling effort per cell, calculated as trap-nights (i.e., the number of active deployments times the duration they were active, in days).

samplingStart

The earliest deploymentStart date-time among the deployments in a cell, marking the beginning of the sampling period per cellID.

samplingEnd

The latest deploymentEnd date-time among the deployments in a cell, marking the end of the sampling period per cellID.

Resampled Observations include:

deploymentsActiveAtDate

A concatenated string of deploymentID values that were active in a given resampled cellID on each day.

numberDeploymentsActiveAtDate

The number of deployments active in a given resampled cell on each day.

independentEvents

The total count of unique eventID values per cell per day per species, representing independent events.

independentObservations

The total count of unique observationID values per cell per day per species.

totalIndividuals

The aggregated count of individuals per cell per day per species, computed based on the individuals parameter (either by summing counts or taking the maximum value).

Usage

resample_covariates_and_observations(
  covs,
  obs = NULL,
  individuals,
  mode_cols_covs,
  obs_covs,
  weights = c("camera_days", "none")
)

Arguments

covs

A data frame or tibble of covariate data from a camtrapDP formatted frictionless data package, which can be accessed from the WildObsR::wildobs_dp_download() function. It must include columns defining spatial cells (with names starting with "cellID"), and date-time columns (e.g., deploymentStart and deploymentEnd) formatted as POSIXct.

obs

A data frame or tibble of observation data from a camtrapDP formatted frictionless data package, which can be accessed from the WildObsR::wildobs_dp_download() function. It must include a deploymentID column and several date-time columns (e.g., eventStart, eventEnd, classificationTimestamp formatted as POSIXct. Or NULL (default) to resample the covariates only; individuals and obs_covs are then not used.

individuals

A character string specifying how to aggregate the number of individuals counted per spatially re sampled cell per day. Options are "sum" to take the sum total number of counts or "max" to use the maximum count. "sum" adds the count of every observation of the species in the cell that day, across all its cameras and repeat triggers, so one cat triggering a camera three times in 10 minutes counts 3, and a cat passing two cameras counts 2: an index of animal detections, not a number of individuals. "max" is the most individuals in a single observation, a conservative minimum present. This only affects the resampled observations; detection_matrix() counts from the observations themselves, with its own individuals.

mode_cols_covs

(Optional) A character vector specifying the names of covariate columns for which the mode should be computed rather than concatenating all unique values. (Example: c("habitat")). With weights = "camera_days", the mode is the value covering the most camera-days in the cell.

obs_covs

(Optional) A character vector specifying observation-level covariate column names that may vary in space and time and will be combined with the resampled observations. (Example: c("baitUse", "featureType")). These are used only by matrix_generator(); for detection covariates with effort_matrix(), use its split_by instead.

weights

How each deployment counts towards its cell's averaged (Avg_*) and modal (mode_*) covariates. "camera_days" (default) weights each deployment by how long it ran, deploymentEnd - deploymentStart in days; "none" counts every deployment once, the plain mean and most frequent value. See "Weighting by camera-days".

Value

A nested list with two elements:

spatially_resampled_observations

A list of data frames corresponding to different spatial scales (e.g., "cellID_1km", "cellID_10km") containing all resampled observation data. Left out when obs = NULL.

spatially_resampled_covariates

A list of data frames corresponding to different spatial scales containing all resampled covariate data, one row per cell.

Each table carries a wildobs_resampled attribute naming its scale, so effort_matrix() and detection_matrix() can recognise them and say what to pass instead.

Details

The function performs the following steps to resample the covariate and observation data:

  1. Data Validation:

    • Verifies that the covariates data frame contains at least one spatial cellID column generated from the WildObsR::spatial_hexagon_generator() function (i.e., a column whose name starts with "cellID"). If not, the function stops with an error.

    • Checks that the deploymentID values match between the covariates and observation data. If there is a mismatch, the function stops with an error.

    • Ensures that the specified observation-level covariate columns (provided in obs_covs) exist in the covariates data. If some are missing, they are omitted from further processing with a warning.

    • Confirms that all required date-time columns in both datasets are formatted as POSIXct. This includes columns such as eventStart, eventEnd, and classificationTimestamp in the observations, and deploymentStart and deploymentEnd in the covariates.

  2. Data Preparation:

    • Removes any columns that contain only NA values from both datasets.

    • For the covariates:

      • Extracts character columns (excluding those that will be processed by mode aggregation) and numeric columns that will be averaged.

      • Adds sequential Julian date values derived from deploymentStart and deploymentEnd to standardize the temporal resolution. These columns are removed before returning the final datasets.

    • For the observations:

      • Extracts date-time columns (identified by the POSIXct class), character/factor columns, and numeric columns (excluding those with names like "deltaTime" or "count").

      • Computes a sequential Julian date from eventStart to serve as the daily resolution for resampling. This column is removed before returning the final datasets.

  3. Resampling by Deployment Group and Spatial Scale:

    • The function loops over each unique deploymentGroup present in the covariates data. This speeds up the process.

    • For each deploymentGroup:

      • Subsets the covariates and observations to include only the relevant deployments.

      • Merges spatial cell information (i.e., the cellID columns) from the covariates into the observations based on the deploymentID.

  4. Resampling of Covariates:

    • Within each deploymentGroup, the function iterates over each spatial scale (columns containing "cellID_").

    • For each spatial scale, it loops through each unique sampling unit (i.e., each unique cell value):

      • A new row is created for each sampling unit, starting as an empty data frame with the same structure as the covariates data.

      • Numeric covariate values are aggregated by computing the mean, weighted by camera-days unless weights = "none" (or left as NA if all values are missing). The column names are updated to indicate that these are averaged values (e.g., "Avg_<column>").

      • Sampling effort is calculated as the total active duration (in days) summed over all unique deployments in the cell.

      • The sampling period is defined by the minimum deploymentStart (as samplingStart) and maximum deploymentEnd (as samplingEnd) for the cell.

      • Character variables are processed by pasting together sorted unique values.

      • For any covariate specified in mode_cols_covs, the function calculates the mode (the value covering the most camera-days, or the most frequent value with weights = "none") instead of concatenating all values.

      • Spatial information is preserved by keeping the cell identifier and any associated polygon geometry.

  5. Resampling of Observations:

    • For each spatial scale, the function further processes the observations by iterating over each sampling unit, each day (based on the sequential Julian date), and each species (scientificName).

    • For each combination:

      • The function merges relevant observation-level covariate information from the covariates dataset.

      • Date-time columns are aggregated: start times are set to the minimum value and end times to the maximum.

      • Active deployment information is compiled, including a concatenated list of active deployments and the count of these deployments.

      • Event-level metrics are computed, such as the number of unique events and observations.

      • Individual counts are aggregated according to the user-specified method (either "sum" or "max").

      • Species-level variables are aggregated by concatenating sorted unique values.

      • Numeric observation columns are averaged.

  6. Compilation of Resampled Data:

    • After processing all deploymentGroups and spatial scales, a final verification is implemented to ensure all cellID values are present and matching in the resampled covariates and observations.

    • Finally, the function assembles the resampled data into two nested lists:

      • One list contains the resampled covariates, organized by spatial scale.

      • The other list contains the resampled observations, also organized by spatial scale.

  7. Output:

    • The function returns a single list with two elements:

      • "spatially resampled observations": a nested list of data frames for each spatial scale.

      • "spatially resampled covariates": a nested list of data frames for each spatial scale.

How the tables connect

The occupancy and abundance workflow uses three tables, each at the level its function needs, joined by two keys: deploymentID links observations to deployments, and the cellID column (for example cellID_3km2) links deployments to cells.

TableOne row perMade byGoes into
Deployments with cellIDs (covs_cellID)deploymentspatial_hexagon_generator()effort_matrix() with site_col = "cellID_3km2"
Observationsobservationfrictionless::read_resource()detection_matrix(), which places each one in its cell through the effort matrix
Cell covariatescellthis function, with obs = NULLmodel_matrix_input() as site_covs

Effort needs each camera's own start and end, which only the deployment table keeps, so the resampled covariates are used for site covariates only. The resampled observations are for matrix_generator() and for summaries per cell and day.

Weighting by camera-days

A covariate that does not change over time, such as elevation, still differs between the cameras in a cell, and the cell's value is an average over them. Weighting by camera-days makes that average describe the habitat the cameras actually sampled, the same camera-days the effort and detections come from. Two examples:

  • Camera A at 200 m ran 90 days; camera B at 800 m failed after 2 days. The plain mean is 500 m; the weighted mean is (200 x 90 + 800 x 2) / 92 = 213 m, where nearly all the detections came from.

  • Station X at 200 m was redeployed four times for 25 days each; station Y at 800 m ran once for 100 days. The plain mean over the five rows is 320 m, counting X four times only because its cards were changed more often; the weighted mean is 500 m, treating both stations' equal effort equally.

When the cameras in a cell ran for similar lengths the two agree closely: on three public WildObs projects at 3 km² cells, weighting moved values by a median of under 5% of the spread between cameras in the same cell. The difference matters for failed cameras, redeployed stations and large cells.

Coordinates (latitude, longitude) are always plain means, since they describe where the cameras are rather than what they sampled. A deployment with a missing or negative length has no weight; a cell where no deployment has any falls back to the plain mean, with a warning. cellEffort is unaffected: it is always the total camera-days.

Zachary Amir

Examples

# load the Woomargama wombat project shipped with WildObsR
dp <- example_datapackages("NSW_Woomargama_wombats_Linley_2021-22_WildObsID_0010")[[1]]

# extract one table of deployments and their covariates
deps <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "deployments")
covs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "covariates")
# merge both tables together based on several shared columns 
covs <- merge(deps, covs, by = intersect(names(deps), names(covs)))

# assign every camera to a 1 km2 hexagonal cell (scales are cell areas in m2)
covs_cellID <- spatial_hexagon_generator(covs, scales = 1e6)

# for occupancy and abundance models, resample the covariates only: one row per cell
cell <- resample_covariates_and_observations(covs_cellID, mode_cols_covs = "baitUse")
cell_covs <- cell$spatially_resampled_covariates$cellID_1km2
head(cell_covs[, c("cellID_1km2", "cellEffort", "mode_baitUse")])
#>                                           cellID_1km2 cellEffort mode_baitUse
#> 1 Woomargama_NP_177_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010   190.5010        FALSE
#> 2 Woomargama_NP_183_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010   191.9194        FALSE
#> 3 Woomargama_NP_130_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010   188.6898        FALSE
#> 4 Woomargama_NP_124_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010   187.9236        FALSE
#> 5  Woomargama_NP_11_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010   192.9283        FALSE
#> 6  Woomargama_NP_23_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010   196.2188        FALSE

# observations that can be placed on a camera (obscured records cannot)
obs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "observations")
obs <- obs[obs$deploymentID %in% covs_cellID$deploymentID, ]

# or resample the observations to cells and days too, for matrix_generator() or summaries
resamp <- resample_covariates_and_observations(covs_cellID, obs, individuals = "sum",
                                               obs_covs = c("baitUse", "featureType"))
#> Warning: resample_covariates_and_observations() found sampled cells with no observations:
#>   Woomargama_NP_2022_b_Linley_WildObsID_0010 at cellID_1km2: 1 of 27 cells
#> This is expected when obs is filtered to a few species, or when a cell detected nothing: the cells stay in the resampled covariates, and effort_matrix() and matrix_generator() count them as sampled with no detections (zeros). It is a problem if obs was filtered by deployment, date or observationType in a way that removed real records, since those zeros would then be false absences. Check that obs covers every deployment in covs.
#> resample_covariates_and_observations(): lifeStage (e.g. "adult - juvenile"), sex (e.g. "female - male") kept as text, because some cells hold more than one value.
#> For one value per cell, add the column to mode_cols_covs; to model detection by it, use effort_matrix(split_by = ...).
head(resamp$spatially_resampled_observations$cellID_1km2[, c("cellID_1km2", "scientificName",
                                                             "totalIndividuals")])
#>                                           cellID_1km2        scientificName
#> 1 Woomargama_NP_177_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010 Trichosurus vulpecula
#> 2 Woomargama_NP_177_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010 Trichosurus vulpecula
#> 3 Woomargama_NP_177_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010      Vombatus ursinus
#> 4 Woomargama_NP_177_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010 Trichosurus vulpecula
#> 5 Woomargama_NP_177_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010      Vombatus ursinus
#> 6 Woomargama_NP_177_cellID_1km2_2021_a_WildObsID_0010      Vombatus ursinus
#>   totalIndividuals
#> 1                1
#> 2                3
#> 3                1
#> 4                1
#> 5                1
